correctness.rationale: Orthogonality of disk Poisson harmonic modes under the complex Wirtinger-gradient normalization gives ψα(n)=n²B(n,α+1). For 0<α≤1 the positive mixing density να(dt)=α(1-αt)(1-t)^(α-2)dt satisfies ψα(n+1)-ψα(n)=∫t^n(1-t)να(dt), hence ψα(n)=∫(1-t^n)να(dt); Poisson Fourier coefficients establish the positive boundary-jump formula. α=0 follows from the classical circular H^1/2 Dirichlet formula. For α>1, ψα(n)→0 despite ψα(1)>0; averaging 1-cos(nθ) over all n tends to 1 off the diagonal, and Fatou rules out any positive, even nonstationary J. At α=1, να=dt gives total jump activity exactly one and j1(θ) as the displayed elementary formula; α<1 has infinite activity and derived sharp small-angle density. Increment positivity proves the positive spectral gap 1/(1+α). Independent 45 exact beta-increment checks (after expanding special functions), and numerical direct quadrature of j1 at four distinct angles agree; checks supplement full proof.

value.rationale: The positive-jump representability of a canonical one-parameter family of weighted harmonic energies is a natural classification question explicitly motivated by the cited general theory. The α=1 transition from infinite to finite jump activity identifies an exact process-level boundary, while the converse excludes all positive kernels for α>1 even without symmetry. The special-family classification gives useful structural information beyond prior sufficiency.
